slides.title: What’s Data Visualization “Data visualization is an interdisciplinary
slides.text: What’s Data Visualization “Data visualization is an interdisciplinary field that deals with the graphic representation of data. ”--Wikipidia

slides.title: Why Data Visualization? Answer questions about your data
slides.text: Why Data Visualization? Answer questions about your data Make decisions Find patterns Present an argument or to tell a story

slides.title: Data Visualization Design Process Understand the context Eliminate
slides.text: Data Visualization Design Process Understand the context Eliminate clutter Think like a designer Draw attention where you want it Choose effective visuals Tell a story with data

slides.title: Understanding the Context Whom are you communicating? What
slides.text: Understanding the Context Whom are you communicating? What do you want your audience to know or do? How can you use data to help make decisions?

slides.title: Understanding the Context Who? “The budget committee that
slides.text: Understanding the Context Who? “The budget  committee that can approve funding for continuation of the Summer learning program.” What “The summer learning program on science was a success, please approve budget of $X to continue.” How “Illustrate success with data collected through the survey conducted before and after the pilot program”

slides.title: Choosing Effective Visuals
slides.text: Choosing Effective Visuals

slides.title: Simple Text VS Use simple text when you
slides.text: Simple Text VS Use simple text when you just have a number or two to share, simple text can be a great way to communicate.

slides.title: Tables Use table when communicate to a mixed
slides.text: Tables Use table when communicate to a mixed audience whose members will each look for their particular row of interest. OR Need to communicate multiple different units of measure. The data should stand out, not the borders

slides.title: Heatmap Use heatmap to help our eyes and
slides.text: Heatmap Use heatmap to help our eyes and brains more quickly target the potential points of interest.

slides.title: Scatter plot Use scatterplots when you need to
slides.text: Scatter plot Use scatterplots when you need to show the relationship between two things.

slides.title: Line Line graphs are most commonly used to
slides.text: Line Line graphs are most commonly used to plot continuous data.

slides.title: Slopegraph Slopegraphs can be useful when you have
slides.text: Slopegraph Slopegraphs can be useful when you have two time periods or points of comparison and want to quickly show relative increases and decreases or differences across various categories between the two data points.

slides.title: Vertical Bar Chart Vertical bar chart is easy
slides.text: Vertical Bar Chart Vertical bar chart is easy for our eyes to read. Must have zero baseline! Be cautious with multiple series

slides.title: Stacked Vertical Bar Use stacked vertical bar to
slides.text: Stacked Vertical Bar Use stacked vertical bar to compare totals across categories and also see the subcomponent pieces within a given category. (limited use cases)

slides.title: Waterfall Use waterfall chart to pull apart the
slides.text: Waterfall Use waterfall chart to pull apart the pieces of a stacked bar chart to focus on one at a time, or to show a starting point, increases and decreases, and the resulting ending point.

slides.title: Horizontal Bar The go-to graph for categorical data.
slides.text: Horizontal Bar The go-to graph for categorical data. Extremely easy to read . Be cautious with multiple series

slides.title: Staked Horizontal Bar Use staked horizontal bar to
slides.text: Staked Horizontal Bar Use staked horizontal bar to show the totals across different categories but also give a sense of the subcomponent pieces. (better than staked vertical bar due to consistent baseline on the left and right)

slides.title: Square Area Try to avoid square area unless
slides.text: Square Area Try to avoid square area unless when you need to visualize numbers of vastly different magnitudes.

slides.title: Ethics and Data Visualization Intentional or unintentional use
slides.text: Ethics and Data Visualization Intentional or unintentional use of deceptive techniques with the potential of altering the audience's understanding of the information being presented.
